name: CI environment
description: Where the build is running: which CI provider, whether the runner is hosted or self hosted, what triggered it, and whether federated credentials are available to it.

envFile.description: Read the environment from this `KEY=VALUE` file instead of the process environment. Meant for testing a guardrail against a runner you are not on.

facts.ci: Whether the build is running on a CI runner at all, as opposed to a developer's workstation.
facts.provider: CI provider recognised from its own variables: `github`, `gitlab`, `jenkins`, `azure`, `circle`, `buildkite`, `teamcity`, `bitbucket`, `drone`, `travis`, or `local` when none is recognised.
facts.hosted: Whether the runner is the provider's own hosted fleet. `false` for a self hosted runner, `null` when the provider does not say.
facts.trigger: What started the build, as the provider names it, or `null`.
facts.pullRequest: Whether the build is for a pull or merge request.
facts.fork: Whether that request came from a fork, `null` when the provider does not say. A fork build is the one that must run without secrets.
facts.runner.os: Operating system the runner reports, or `null`.
facts.runner.name: Name the runner reports, or `null`.
facts.oidc: Whether a federated identity token is available to this job, so a pipeline can reach a cloud without a long lived key.
facts.variables: Names of the CI variables that were set. Names only, never values: the facts are attached to the run event and a value can be a credential.
